title: Spend Sentry: Client Usage Audit & QBR Worksheet (draft)
content:
Purpose: Quick, repeatable worksheet for Customer Success to audit token spend, rate limits, and budget alerts ahead of renewal conversations and QBRs. Designed to produce a 10–15 minute summary slide + a small set of action items for ops/eng.

Notes/context (working):
- This is a working doc: use for pre-QBR prep calls, week-of health checks, and post-QBR followups.
- Goal is to move away from raw token tables and towards signalized issues (cost regressions, burst risk, throttling exposure).
- Keep thresholds opinionated but adjustable per-customer category (startup, scale, enterprise).

Key outputs for the QBR slide deck (1 page):
1) Top-line: 30/90-day token trend (tokens/day, tokens/active-user) with % change.
2) Risk summary: any active budget alerts, recent rate limit events, and projected 30-day spend runway.
3) Recommendation: 1–2 ops/eng actions + suggested guardrail (e.g., soft cap, revised quota, batching suggestion).

How to use this sheet (quick workflow):
1) Pull last 90 days of usage by route & model variant for account X.
2) Compute median tokens/request, p95 latency, and cost per thousand tokens (unit cost).
3) Run the heuristics section below to flag anomalies.
4) Fill the quick summary and propose 1 ops ticket + 1 customer recommendation.

Required data pulls (queries/examples):
- Usage summary (SQL pseudo):
  SELECT date, route, model_variant, sum(requests) AS calls, sum(tokens_in + tokens_out) AS tokens
  FROM inference_usage
  WHERE account_id = :acct AND date >= current_date - interval '90 days'
  GROUP BY date, route, model_variant
  ORDER BY date;

- Rate limit events:
  SELECT timestamp, route, error_code, quota_bucket, count(*) AS events
  FROM rate_limit_logs
  WHERE account_id = :acct AND timestamp >= current_date - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY timestamp, route, error_code, quota_bucket
  ORDER BY timestamp DESC;

- Budget alert checks (API): pull alerts from Billing Alerts table and compare active = true

Heuristics / Flagging rules (defaults — tune per customer):
- Cost regression: 30-day avg cost per token > 1.25x 90-day avg => flag as COST_REGRESSION.
- Burst risk: any day with tokens > 3x 30-day median => flag as BURST_EVENT.
- Rate-pressure: > 5 rate-limit events in last 7 days across any route => RATE_PRESSURE.
- Runway warning: projected 30-day spend given trailing 7-day avg > committed budget remaining => BUDGET_RUNWAY_LOW.
- Efficiency drop: median tokens per completion increased > 20% with no model change => EFF_DROP

Suggested threshold tiers (examples):
- Startup (low budget): cost_regression multiplier 1.15, burst factor 2.5, rate_limit_count 3
- Scale: multiplier 1.25, burst factor 3, rate_limit_count 5
- Enterprise: multiplier 1.4, burst 4, rate_limit_count 8

Soft vs Hard alerts (customer-facing play):
- Soft alert: automated email to customer-success + customer if runway < 30 days, include suggested quick mitigations (batching, reduce token limit, lower temp).
- Hard alert: if active spending > 120% of committed/forecast and rate-limit events causing errors -> escalate to accounts + sales ops for potential invoice/contract refresh.

Checklist (pre-QBR):
- [ ] Pull 90d usage & last 30d rate-limit logs (owner: CS AE).
- [ ] Run heuristics and mark any flags (owner: CS analyst).
- [ ] Draft 1-slide summary + 2 recommended actions (owner: CS AE).
- [ ] If BUDGET_RUNWAY_LOW or RATE_PRESSURE, open ops ticket and cc ENG on on-call (owner: CS AE).
- [ ] Add notes to renewal tracker if spend trend intersects renewal window (owner: CS AE).

Playbook: actions mapped to flags
- COST_REGRESSION -> action: run token-level diff by route; suggest quantization/cheaper model variant; propose 2-week cost guard. (owner: CS + Solutions Eng)
- BURST_EVENT -> action: identify source route, propose rate-limiting rules or client-side batching; consider temporary burst quota for a 2-week window. (owner: Solutions Eng)
- RATE_PRESSURE -> action: verify if rate limits are client-imposed or infra; if infra, triage with SRE and request capacity bump. (owner: Eng SRE + CS)
- BUDGET_RUNWAY_LOW -> action: recommend soft cap and auto-notify to customer; if near renewal, prep contract amendment options. (owner: Accounts + CS)
quick_summary:
Account: <account-name>
Category: scale
90-day tokens: 18.2M
30-day avg/day: 210k (↑ 34% vs prior 30d)
Active flags: COST_REGRESSION, RATE_PRESSURE
Projected 30d spend @ current pace: $12,400 (committed remaining: $9,000) -> RUNWAY_LOW
recent_events:
2026-02-18: 17 rate-limit events on /v1/generate (bursting during nightly jobs)
2026-02-22: Budget alert (email) fired when spend crossed 85% of monthly forecast
2026-02-26: Customer reported intermittent 429s during peak hour (correlates with rate-limit logs)
recommended_actions:
1) Create ENG ticket (on-call) to look at /v1/generate 429 stack traces + enable granular rate-limiting by client-id (owner: Ethan)
2) Suggest customer switch non-critical routes to cheaper model variant (4k -> 1.5k) and enable prefix-caching (owner: Solutions Eng)
3) Add 30-day soft cap at $10k with escalation workflow to customer (owner: Accounts)
open_questions_and_todo:
- Confirm whether nightly job is server-side retrying (CS to ask dev contact)
- Is the customer open to model variant trade-offs? (ask in pre-QBR)
- If we offer temporary burst quota, what is expected billback policy? (finance check: FIN-472)

Notes to self:
- Keep the spreadsheet view narrow: route/model_date | tokens | median_latency | p95_latency | rate_limit_events | cost
- Use the 'heuristics' sheet to store per-account multipliers so we can tune without changing logic

Slack links/references:
- slack:#cs-account-x -> thread: "payment-alerts-2/26"
- slack:#eng-sre oncall -> incident ref: INC-2026-023

Appendix: suggested customer language for soft cap email (short):
"Hi <name>,
We noticed an unexpected increase in token usage on a few routes which may cause your monthly spend to exceed your forecast. We recommend a short-term cap to prevent surprises and a few low-effort changes that could reduce cost (switching non-customer-facing jobs to a lower-cost model, enabling simple caching). Happy to walk through options on the QBR.
Best, Maya (CS)"

Version history (tracking in this doc):
- 2025-11-04: initial skeleton (Maya)
- 2026-01-15: added heuristics and SQL examples (Liam)
- 2026-02-28: tuned thresholds after 3 pilot accounts (Sofia)

END OF WORKSHEET
